# pin / pin_differ

Duress PIN differ — the PIN pill is scanned, rejected by a shake.

**PORT** — the device implements this.

> Duress PIN differ — the PIN pill is scanned, rejected by a shake.
>
> Port of pin_differ.py, all in colors.ORANGE (state="warning"; the
> source's #FF9B3D corrected to the palette). The pill outline fades in,
> the four dots land, a beat, then a black-stroked scanline sweeps
> forward-back-forward across the pill and fades; the row shakes off the
> duress PIN and the caption names the rule. Not a verdict — the pill row
> is the whole picture, so it runs its own timeline on StatusAnim; the
> verdict twin (screens/verdict/duress_differ.py) states the same rule on
> the verdict law, and both draw the same art, pq1.procedural.pin_pill.
>
>     hold 250 -> fill 200 -> hold 200 -> scan 975 -> shake 420
>              -> caption 300                               t_resolve 2345
>
> Paced with that twin (user, Sep 2026): the same 200 ms fill and beats,
> the same 325 ms per scanline traverse — three of them here, for this
> screen's 1.5-cycle sweep — and the same 210 ms shake cycle. Every phase
> clears VERDICT_ACCENT_MIN_MS (145 ms, two frames at the panel's 14 fps)
> with room to spare, so no beat reads as rushed on the device.

The same rule as [verdict / duress_differ](verdict-duress-differ.md), stated as a plain `pin`-category
screen instead of a verdict. The difference is the opening and the sweep, not the message: here the
pill fades in flat — **no black hold, no rise, no entrance law** — and the scanline crosses the pill
three times instead of two, so it ends at the far side rather than back where it began.

Both draw the same art, `pq1.procedural.pin_pill` (`pq1/procedural/pin_pill.py:33`), in the
warning orange 245 160 51, and their resting frames are pixel-identical. Write the pill, the sweep and
the shake ONCE and give them the two openings as parameters: the verdict twin when a token hands over
to it, this one when the pill is already the whole picture.

## Timeline

Play order; no presets, so one table. Every offset is absolute — this module lays its phases out as
`T0_*` start times from t 0 (`screens/pin/pin_differ.py:40`), not on a mechanism clock.

| phase | ms | frames @14 fps | easing | token | defined at | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| the pill outline fades in | 250 | 3.5 | ease | `T_HOLD` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:31` | alpha 0 to 1 on the outline alone, from t 0. Despite the name this is NOT a black hold: the pill is drawn from the first frame, and there is no scale rise |
| the four dots fade in together | 200 | 2.8 | ease | `T_FILL` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:32` | starts at `T0_FILL` 250. One alpha for all 4 dots, already in the state colour — nothing turns later |
| the full row pauses | 200 | 2.8 | hold | `T_FILLED` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:33` | starts at `T0_FILLED` 450. The beat before the check |
| the scanline sweeps forward, back, forward | 975 | 13.7 | raised cosine | `T_SCAN` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:33` | starts at `T0_SCAN` 650. Position is 0.5 − 0.5·cos(2π·u·cycles) with 1.5 cycles: three traverses of 92 px, each a third of this, ending at the far end |
| … and the bar fades out over the sweep's tail | 97.5 | 1.4 | ease_out | `T_SCAN * SCAN_FADE` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:33` | the last tenth of the sweep — the fraction is `SCAN_FADE` 0.1. Still under two panel frames, so the bar effectively cuts out |
| the row shakes the duress PIN off | 420 | 5.9 | shake | `T_SHAKE` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:33` | starts at `T0_SHAKE` 1625, exactly where the scanline stops being drawn. Centre x moves by 7 px times a decaying sine of 2 cycles — about 6.1 px on the first swing, nothing by the end |
| the caption fades in | 300 | 4.2 | ease_out | `T_TEXT` | `screens/pin/pin_differ.py:33` | starts at `T0_TEXT` 2045, the instant the shake ends. There is NO verdict beat here — the twin inserts one |
| the screen rests | 2450 | 34.3 | hold | `RESULT_HOLD_MS` | `pq1/status.py:101` | from `t_resolve` 2345 to the end |

The shake's progress is clamped, so the pill sits exactly on centre once the shake is spent — the
offset never leaves a residue. `rests_on_token` is false: the pill owns the canvas, no token disc is
drawn, and the flow fades this frame out when it leaves.


Used in: _no live flow yet._

Note the `handoff` key in that spec: `screens.spec()` sets it on every library screen, but this
screen's `draw` never calls the handoff helper, so an incoming token is **not** crossfaded out — it
is simply gone from the first frame. The verdict twin does draw it. If a port wants a hand-over into
this screen, it has to add one.

## Do / Don't

- **Do** start the pill visible. There is no black beat to hide behind: the outline is on screen at
  t 0 and fades up in place.
- **Do** end the sweep at the far side. Three traverses say *scanned end to end*; coming home is the
  verdict twin's reading.
- **Don't** write the pill twice. Only the opening (a black hold and the entrance law, or a flat
  fade) and the sweep's cycle count differ; everything else is shared.
- **Don't** insert a beat before the caption to match the twin. The words land on the pill as the
  shake dies out, and the shake's decay was paced for exactly that overlap.

## Port notes

- **Time is milliseconds, never frames.** Every animation here is a pure function of elapsed ms; the panel samples it at 14 fps. Do not count frames on the device — keep the ms clock and let the frame rate fall where it falls.
- The numbers on this page are read from the running Python at build time. If the page and the code ever disagree, the code wins — then run `python3 -m tools.handoff --check`.
- No one-shot accent is shorter than `VERDICT_ACCENT_MIN_MS` 145 ms (2.0 f) — two panel frames — or the panel may never show it.
